messages:
lucy: Heads up: integration test surfaced odd pacing after 429s — our async client retries on Retry-After (seconds) but ignores X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch or http-date). Leads to small waits then a huge burst when reset happens.
raj: can you paste a concrete header case?
lucy: sure, saw two variants in logs: 
Case A: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: Wed, 18 Jan 2026 15:05:00 GMT
```
Case B: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1772068800
```
lucy: client path: if Retry-After present -> sleep(int), else exponential backoff. Because Reset is later, we end up doing short sleeps and then all clients hit the window.
honor: we need a deterministic precedence: prefer X-RateLimit-Reset (parse epoch or HTTP-date) -> compute delta = reset_ts - now, if delta > 0 then sleep(delta) else if Retry-After present use that -> else fallback to exponential+jitter.
raj: agree. Also normalize header names (lowercase) and handle floats in Retry-After.
kevin: for async ergonomics, propose a small public util at devex.rate limiting: parse_rate_headers(headers) -> {"remaining": Optional[int], "reset_ts": Optional[int], "retry_after": Optional[float]} (TypedDict). And an AsyncRateGuard.wait_if_needed(headers, now_fn=...) coroutine.
lucy: API sketch: ```python
Parsed = TypedDict("Parsed", {"remaining": Optional[int], "reset_ts": Optional[int], "retry_after": Optional[float]})
def parse_rate_headers(headers: Mapping[str,str]) -> Parsed: ...
class AsyncRateGuard:
    def __init__(self, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time): ...
    async def wait_if_needed(self, headers: Mapping[str,str]) -> None: ...
```
kevin: keep the public surface tiny: parse + guard.wait_if_needed. Client.request will call await guard.wait_if_needed(resp.headers) before retrying. Also provide a sync wrapper for blocking client.
honor: testing matrix: (1) only Retry-After, (2) only Reset epoch, (3) only Reset HTTP-date, (4) both present where Retry-After < Reset, (5) both present where Retry-After > Reset, (6) missing headers. Add property tests for monotonic now_fn to simulate time.
raj: edge case: server might send past reset (reset_ts < now) with Retry-After present — should honor Retry-After if positive, otherwise continue.
lucy: good catch. Also document that Reset is server-side epoch seconds OR HTTP-date; attempt int() parse first, then parse HTTP-date with email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime.
kevin: think about rate-limit buckets per-route/key. Guard should accept an optional bucket key so apps can coordinate across concurrent tasks. Not in first PR maybe.
honor: agree keep first PR minimal. Add type annotations + mypy stubs. We'll add unit tests + small integration that hits mirror that returns controlled headers.
ci-bot: CI: pipeline started for branch "devex/async-rate-guard" (PR #4456) :gear: checks pending.
lucy: I'll draft the PR today. Assigning to honor for unit tests and raj for client integration.
kevin: when you open PR ping me for design review. Also include small changelog entry for SDK users.
lucy: thanks all, should reduce the burst problems in Canary.
